entry.title: Improving Next.js Performance: SSR to SSG + ISR for Faster Load Times
entry.summary:
Optimizing performance in Next.js isn’t just about good development practices — it directly affects SEO, user engagement, and Core Web Vitals. Google now considers page speed and interaction delays as ranking factors, and websites using slow server-side rendering may fall behind. When using getServerSideProps, each page request initiates a server call — usually involving database queries or API fetches. While this is ideal for dynamic content, even small delays (150–250ms) hurt TTFB and First Contentful Paint (FCP). Tools like Lighthouse and PageSpeed Insights will show this slow response time front and center in your audits. To solve these delays, we transitioned our pages to getStaticProps with Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR). SSG renders HTML at build time, and ISR allows automatic regeneration every few minutes or hours — combining performance with flexibility. export async function getStaticProps() {
ISR ensures visitors get fast pages, while updates happen behind the scenes. One challenge we hit: Vercel’s 45-minute build time limit (Docs). For websites with thousands of pages, SSG meant long build times. To fix it, we wrote a Node.js script that: Fetches content in parallel Saves data as flat JSON during the build Reads those JSON files in getStaticProps That dropped our build from 65+ minutes to under 30. Lighthouse scores jumped from 75 to 95+ TTFB under 200ms More pages crawled in Google Search Console Lower bounce rates If you're running a growing content site, switching from SSR to SSG + ISR using Next.js best practices can be one of your biggest SEO wins.
